one_liner: Express 4 API re-implemented on uWebSockets.js; README shows 3-12x Express req/s, but Node 24 narrows most gaps.
what_it_does: Ultimate Express (µExpress) re-implements the Express 4 API (it is not a fork) on top of the uWebSockets.js native HTTP server instead of node:http. Migration is meant to be changing require("express") to require("ultimate-express"): app/Router/req/res, express.static/json/urlencoded/text/raw, view engines and common middleware (helmet, cors, passport, multer, express-session, morgan, ...) are covered, and the test suite runs every test against real Express first and compares the output. You never create an http.Server yourself: app.listen() starts uWS, TLS and HTTP/3 are configured through express({ uwsOptions, http3 }), and WebSockets go through app.uwsApp or the sister library Ultimate WS.
how_it_is_fast: HTTP parsing, socket I/O and response writes run in uWebSockets.js (C++ via N-API); responses are written inside res.cork() batches with tryEnd/onWritable backpressure instead of Node's stream stack. At listen(), every route whose path is a plain string (no ':' params and no regex characters) under case-sensitive routing is registered on the native uWS router, with the middleware that matches it resolved once ahead of time; Express instead scans its layer stack on every request, which is why the 1000-route test shows the largest gain (about 11x). A handler simple enough to pass an acorn parse of its source (only res.set/status/send/end with req.query/req.params, no variables, calls or control flow) is compiled into a uWS DeclarativeResponse that is answered without entering JavaScript. Smaller wins: headers are materialised lazily, query strings go through fast-querystring, bodies are read only for POST/PUT/PATCH, and sendFile/static reads of files under 768 KB run on a worker thread (1 by default).
when_to_use: An existing Express 4 app on Node 22 where per-process routing/dispatch overhead, not the database, limits req/s: the project's CI on Node 22 (April-July 2026) showed 6.3-8.2x Express on hello-world and 1.7-3.7x on express.static.
Large tables of plain string routes (hundreds to thousands of paths without ':' params): routes-1000 stays 7.9-11.9x ahead of Express even in the Node 24 CI runs of 2026-07-30/31.
Apps that must keep the Express 4 middleware and view-engine ecosystem but want HTTP/3 or native uWS WebSockets on the same port without a rewrite to hyper-express or raw uWS.
Linux x64/arm64 (glibc), macOS or Windows x64 deployments on Node 22, 24 or 26, the only targets the pinned uWebSockets.js v20.69.0 ships binaries for.
when_not_to_use: Node 24+ with ordinary handler chains: after the CI moved from Node 22 to 24 (2026-07-30), Express hello-world rose from about 7.6k-11k to 14.6k-43k req/s, while a contributor in #364 says µExpress stayed flat. As a result hello-world fell to 2.6-4.1x, compression-file to 1.0-1.1x, and a 100-middleware chain to 0.53-0.73x (slower than Express). The maintainer opened #364, 'UltimateExpress is officially pointless?', about this.
Large bodies and streaming: in the 2026 CI runs a 512 KB JSON body is 0.89-1.04x and streamed responses are 0.70-1.37x, so there is nothing to gain there.

Anything that instruments or needs node:http: Sentry tracing produces no spans (#286), http.on('upgrade') cannot be used, req.socket is a partial shim, and res.writableEnded never becomes true (#372, breaks pino-http).

Alpine/musl, Bun, odd Node releases (23/25) or Windows arm64: uWebSockets.js is glibc-only, has prebuilt binaries only for Node 22/24/26, and is pulled from GitHub rather than the npm registry (#231, #232, #258).
Express 5 codebases: the target is the Express 4 API (a contributor reports running an Express 5 app on it, but that is not claimed in the README); fulmine.js is the Express 5 variant.

integration.form: module (npm package ultimate-express, plain JavaScript, with a git dependency on the uWebSockets.js native addon)
integration.dependencies: uWebSockets.js v20.69.0 (github: dependency with prebuilt .node binaries), acorn, fast-querystring, fast-zlib, tseep, qs, plus Express helper packages (accepts, cookie, cookie-signature, etag, fresh, mime-types, proxy-addr, range-parser, statuses, type-is, vary, ...)
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js >= 22 (engines field); binaries exist for Node 22, 24 and 26 only. ultimate-express@2.1.0 is the last release for Node 19-21, and the node-v18 tag (1.4.10) covers Node 18.
integration.platforms: Linux x64/arm64 (glibc only; no Alpine/musl), macOS x64/arm64, Windows x64; not Bun
integration.thread_safety: Single event loop per process, as with Express. One worker thread (the 'threads' option, 0 on single-core machines) does file reads and is shared by all app instances. Under node:cluster, worker processes listen on a shared port (uWS non-exclusive listen, from src/application.js); the README does not document multi-process use.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the same Express 4 API and most middleware work after a one-line require change, but routing is case-sensitive by default, the header limit is 4 KB, body parsing only covers POST/PUT/PATCH, there is no http.Server (TLS and HTTP/3 go through uwsOptions), express-async-errors does not work (use app.set('catch async errors', true)), and req.route/req.socket/express.request/express.response are partial

gotchas: Case-sensitive routing is on by default, unlike Express. Turning it off, or using ':param', wildcard or regex paths, drops those routes off the native uWS router onto the slower JS matcher. The README only mentions regex characters; the ':' exclusion is in src/router.js.
uWS caps request headers at 4096 bytes against Node's 16384; apps with large cookies or JWTs need the UWS_HTTP_MAX_HEADERS_SIZE environment variable.

Request bodies are read only for POST, PUT and PATCH. A DELETE, or a GET that carries a body, leaves req.body empty unless you add the method to the 'body methods' setting (the README says reading bodies costs about 15%).

Response extends Writable but end() bypasses Node's Writable state, so writableEnded/writableFinished stay false (#372). Reported quirks include 'close' not firing when no response is sent (#287) and morgan logging 200 where the client got a 304 (#206).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over fulmine.js when the app is on the Express 4 API: fulmine.js is derived from µExpress, targets Express 5 only, and its README says Express 4 users should use ultimate-express. Pick either over Elysia (Bun) when you cannot leave Node.js or rewrite handlers.
verified_claims_summary: The README table (wrk -t1 -c200 -d60, one run, Node.js 20.17.0, Ubuntu 22.04, Ryzen 5 3600, measured around v1.2 in 2024 against an unstated Express 4.x) shows 3.10x (compressed small file) to 11.78x (route 999 of 1000) over Express, with 6.73x on a simple route. The project's own newer CI harness (benchmark/run.js, GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest, Node 24, wrk -t1 -c200 -d20) gave these results at the same commit 77ca8a2 on 2026-07-31: 2.57x hello-world, 11.64x routes-1000, 1.05x compression, and 0.69x (slower) for a 100-middleware chain.
status_note: Maintained by one main author (dimdenGD, 808 commits) with contributors, v2.2.1 released 2026-07-30, about 34k npm downloads a month and Apache-2.0 (plus EXPRESS_LICENSE), but there have been no commits since 2026-07-31, the day the maintainer asked in #364 whether Node 24 made the project pointless.
